why: Work on the needed increments d = target - source. Prefix operations build a non-increasing profile and suffix operations a non-decreasing one, so d must split into those two; reading d's consecutive differences (a difference array) shows every rise must come from suffix starts and every drop from prefix ends.
hints: Only additions are allowed, so look at need[i] = target[i] - source[i]. What shape does a sum of prefix increments have? And of suffix increments?

Prefix ops give a non-increasing profile P, suffix ops a non-decreasing S, with d = P + S. Greedily give S only the rises of d (S grows by max(0, d[i] - d[i-1])); then P = d - S must stay >= 0 and non-increasing.
One pass: total = d[0] + sum of positive rises; fail (-1) if some d[i] < 0 or d[i] - S[i] < 0. O(n), 64-bit values.
pitfalls: Any negative need makes it impossible: there is no decrement.
The cost is d[0] (prefix ops all cover index 0, plus any whole-array ops) plus the sum of rises, not the sum of absolute differences.
Values reach 10^13; Python is fine, but in other languages use 64-bit types.
